plan.reason: All three initial role reports agree on the same fallacy (Slippery Slope), so a round‑robin discussion of the evidence is appropriate to confirm this assessment.

Factual.content: The comment asserts that a single protest will inevitably spiral into increasingly severe outcomes—violent protests, economic collapse, and ultimately a civil war—without providing evidence for that causal chain. This inference of an unproven escalation of events exemplifies a slippery‑slope argument.

Logical.content: I can hardly blame the fine people of Cuba protesting against their government, the leadership of Cuba has been pretty poor for seemingly forever. I do worry that these protests could easily get out of hand though. What starts as one small protest could lead to protest after protest. People could get out of hand, I could even see these protest becoming violent. Citizens could become afraid to even go outside and the economy begins to suffer. Who knows where this could lead, maybe even a civil war as all of society begins to crumble?

Slippery Slope: The comment predicts a chain of escalating consequences—from a small protest to civil war—without any evidence that such a progression is likely. The inference underpinning the fallacy is that protests will inevitably lead to violence, societal collapse, and war.

Evidence: "What starts as one small protest could lead to protest after protest… maybe even a civil war as all of society begins to crumble?"
